req.title: POST-only actions reject GET
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when GET is used on /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: The violation is that test[5] (test_put_delete_also_returns_405) has kind=negative but heuristic=EP. EP (Equivalence Partitioning) is a valid heuristic for negative tests when the test exercises an invalid input partition. However, the rule-based checker flags negative+EP as invalid. To fix this, we change test[5]'s heuristic from EP to NEG, which is the correct heuristic for negative tests that verify rejection of disallowed inputs. All other tests are preserved exactly as they were.

tests.name: test_get_delete_existing_post_returns_405
preconditions: App initialized with test database containing post id=1
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_existing_post_returns_405():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405

test_get_delete_existing_post_returns_405()

tests.name: test_post_delete_authenticated_does_not_return_405
preconditions: App initialized with test database containing post id=1 authored by user id=1 (username=test)
expected: HTTP status code is exactly 302 (redirect), NOT 405
trace: R-FLASKR-030: only GET must return 405; POST is the allowed method and must succeed
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_post_delete_authenticated_does_not_return_405():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 405

test_post_delete_authenticated_does_not_return_405()

tests.name: test_get_delete_unauthenticated_returns_405_not_302
actions: Send GET request to /1/delete without any session cookie
expected: Status code is NOT 302 (no redirect to login before method check)
trace: R-FLASKR-030: Flask method-not-allowed check happens at routing layer before any view decorator (login_required); GET must yield 405 even for anonymous users
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_unauthenticated_returns_405_not_302():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 302
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 403
